effective.acceptance: The report's trace table has one row per requirement of the LOGOS-SERVICE-DISCOVERY specification, in the document's order, each with a file:line in the unit or an explicit 'not in unit' / 'needs external evidence'. Every confirmed code finding has a new test in tests/libp2p/service_discovery/ that fails on the audited commit for the divergence it names. Prose-only findings are marked as such. The target implementation is unchanged.
effective.context:
nim-libp2p is the Nim implementation of libp2p; this audit covers only its Logos service discovery protocol, traced against the LOGOS-SERVICE-DISCOVERY LIP as on the bus. The audited ref is master at a2eb253f1fb755364b3c074eda040b15ed267b8a; record the resolved commit in the report.

Where the protocol lives: libp2p/protocols/service_discovery.nim is the entry module; libp2p/protocols/service_discovery/ holds types.nim (messages, tickets, system parameters), advertiser.nim (ADVERTISE, the advertise table), discoverer.nim (LOOKUP, the search table), registrar.nim (REGISTER and GET_ADS handling, waiting time, the registrar table), advertisement_cache.nim, routing_table_manager.nim (per-service tables and buckets), connection.nim (streams), random_find.nim, dial_backoff.nim, discovery_tracker.nim and service_discovery_metrics.nim; libp2p/extended_peer_record.nim is the signed advertisement. The protocol builds on the Kademlia routing table in libp2p/protocols/kademlia (routing_table.nim, ip_diversity.nim, keyspace.nim), which is outside the unit: read it where a requirement leads there, and mark behaviour that lives only there 'not in unit'. The C bindings in cbind/ are out of scope.

The spec's 'Example ... algorithm' sections, the Appendix and the Implementation Notes are illustrative or recommended; a different algorithm that meets the normative MUST/SHOULD text is not by itself a divergence. Treat code comments that cite the spec as claims to check.

Running tests: tests are Nim unittest files named test_*.nim; tests/test_all.nim imports every test_*.nim under tests/ whose path contains the -d:path substring, so `make test service_discovery` compiles and runs everything under tests/libp2p/service_discovery/ (unit tests there, multi-node tests in component/, shared helpers in utils.nim). The gate puts nim 2.2.14 from /w/cache/nim-2.2.14/bin on PATH and runs `make test service_discovery`; the same works inside the session. Do not use nix: the flake's dev shell ships a nimble too old for the Makefile. New proof tests go in tests/libp2p/service_discovery/ as their own test_*.nim file named by finding id, are picked up with no other edit, and should copy the header and import style of an existing file there (SPDX header, `{.used.}`, the unittest wrapper from tests/tools/unittest). The build uses --styleCheck:error, so follow the existing naming. No external network is available to tests; a proof that needs a live remote peer is 'needs external evidence'.
